newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa pares gains but May revisits 1,000 stg.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa pares gains but May revisits 1,000 stg.

text.p: Cocoa futures mustered enough upside momentum to push off earlier lows on Wednesday as the key May contract clawed its way back through the psychological 1,000 stg a tonne barrier.

London had trouble holding onto its gains with the New York market moving lower in a correction to its recent strength, and May slumped 17 at one stage to 993 stg -- four stg lower than Tuesday's session low.
"There were stops that were touched early in the afternoon which caused the slide...but the volume isn't as big as it has been in previous days," said one trader.
At the close May stood four stg lower at 1,006 stg after trading in a range of 993 to 1,022 stg. July was up three at 1,015 stg and volume amounted to 9,538 lots.
In fundamental news, Ivorian arrivals were reported to be in a range between 920,000 and 960,000 tonnes by March 7, after 940,000 in the record 1995/96 season.
Ivory Coast has forecast a total crop of 950,000 tonnes for 1996/97 but commodities minister Guy-Alain Gauze said this week that it had now sold 800,000 tonnes of cocoa and had no more to sell.
Broker switching was said to have boosted the volume.
But technically, the London market could still have more room to the upside, traders and analysts said.
"You had a breakaway gap, now you have a runaway gap which has been confirmed. Everything still points to much higher levels," said one trader, referring to a gap between 997 and 982 stg basis May.
"A sudden burst of upside energy has taken cocoa prices through overhead supply and, despite extreme over-extension, they could go higher yet," said Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge.
